text:
ana: Heads-up — after the nodepool update I see a 15-30% regression on p99 for the small-chat endpoint. Ran an nsys capture and a quick perf run. Attaching summary and trace name: 1919998888_probe.nsys

matt: which nodepool change? new runtime or kubelet flags?

ana: we tried switching pods to a non-privileged runtime and mounted /dev/nvidia* as read-only hostPaths instead of privileged mounts to satisfy security reqs.

srini: can you paste the nsys summary (top kernels)? any obvious hotspots or long memcpy?

ana: paste from nsys summary:```
Top GPU Kernels (inclusive):
cutlass_gemm   45.1%  1.8s
aten_mm        22.3%  0.9s
memcpy_h2d     10.7%  0.4s
kernel_launch_overhead 8.2% 0.33s
layer_norm_fwd 5.6%  0.22s
other kernels  8.1%  0.32s
```
Also NVTX ranges show spikes coinciding with KV cache misses (we log KV miss events). Timeline shows many small kernel invocations instead of fused batched GEMMs.

matt: that smells like fallback to a less-optimized GEMM kernel. If the toolkit/driver can't access certain device files it sometimes falls back to cuBLAS-lite or a smaller-codepath kernel.

jen: +1. Also check nvidia-container-toolkit version and whether /run/nvidia or /var/lib/nvidia have proper perms. If the runtime can't create symlinks or populate metrics it may degrade behavior.

ana: ran strace on entrypoint (snippet):```
openat(AT_FDCWD, "/var/lib/nvidia/metrics", O_RDONLY) = -1 EACCES (Permission denied)
stat("/run/nvidia/driver", 0x7ffd...) = -1 ENOENT (No such file or directory)
```

srini: okay that's actionable. For test, can you try an initContainer to chown/chmod those paths before the app starts? Example initContainer:```
initContainers:
- name: nvidia-fixperms
  image: busybox
  command: ["sh", "-c", "chown -R 1000:1000 /var/lib/nvidia /run/nvidia || true; chmod -R g+rw /var/lib/nvidia /run/nvidia || true"]
  securityContext:
    runAsUser: 0
  volumeMounts:
  - mountPath: /var/lib/nvidia
    name: nvidia-socket
```
This allowed the toolkit to create its symlinks in my local repro.

deploy-bot: deploy/eng-runtime-perf-test started for revision d4f3a2 — job id perf-191999.

sam: also validate NV_LIBRARY_PATH / LD_PRELOAD / NV_GPU envs. If those aren't propagated into the container (or are blocked by seccomp), the runtime can pick non-optimized codepaths.

ana: quick test: restarted a single pod with a privileged mount and perf went back to baseline p99. So it's permission-related for sure. I'm going to add an initContainer chown + a short e2e perf check in the canary.

matt: cool. Please open an infra PR and tag eng-runtime + eng-ml. Add a small test that runs the small-chat perf harness and asserts p99 <= baseline * 1.05.

jen: add a note in docs: "If you run non-privileged containers, ensure nvidia-container-toolkit can create /run/nvidia symlinks and has write perms to /var/lib/nvidia; otherwise runtime may fall back to smaller GEMM kernels and increase latency."

srini: also idea: add a runtime guard — if KV cache miss rate increases and kernel fingerprint changes between deploys, trigger an automatic rollback or alert. We saw many small kernels when workspace allocation failed.

ana: uploaded full nsys trace to s3: s3://redwood-traces/eng-runtime/1919998888_probe.nsys.qd and perf summary CSV s3://redwood-traces/eng-runtime/1919998888_summary.csv

matt: thanks. After the infra PR lands let's run a few nodepool pods with the initContainer, then run the perf job and close the loop.

ana: will do, creating PR now and tagging folks. Thanks for the quick triage. :thumbsup:
